sn22.62:1.2: The three “scopes” or “ranges” (_patha_) are the past, present, and future, each of which is indicated by the appropriate grammatical tense. | _Nirutti_ means the “clear expression” or “definition” of a word. In the pre-Buddhist literature, that which is “undefined” is the mystical truth to be muttered under the breath, whereas that which is “defined” is clearly expressed in language. A list of such definitions is a _nirukti_, a glossary or dictionary. See [dn15:32.11](), [mn139:13.55](), and [an5.169:3.6]().
sn22.62:13.2: This pair is also mentioned in the same way regarding different teachings at [mn117:38.1]() and especially [an4.30:8.2](), which probably the original context. Nothing is known of them apart from these passages. | Ukkalā lay on the Bay of Bengal in the region today called Odisha. It was the origin of the merchants Tapussa and Bhallika who offered the first meal to the Buddha ([pli-tv-kd1:4.2.1](), [an1.248:1.1]()).
